**Sundhedsreformen** (the health reform) is an upcoming political reform in Denmark that is expected to significantly alter the healthcare landscape, particularly concerning patient transitions between sectors. According to the draft 2026 annual report for the Acute Surgery Database (Akut Kirurgi Databasen), the reform is anticipated to have a major impact on the [[transition-to-primary-care|transition to primary care]] following hospital interventions [^src1]. 

The reform is of particular interest to clinical quality development and surgical outcome monitoring. Specifically, it is expected to become a central factor in future efforts to reduce mortality in the critical period between day 30 and day 90 after acute surgical procedures [^src1]. As the healthcare system prepares for these structural changes, the Acute Surgery Database report emphasizes the need to evaluate and methodologically adjust quality indicators—such as Indicator 10, which tracks 90-day mortality for operated patients—to ensure robustness and comparability across regions [^src1]. 

Furthermore, the implementation of the reform has prompted discussions about the necessity of new process indicators. These indicators are deemed essential for monitoring and ensuring effective collaboration between hospitals and the primary care sector, especially as hospitals anticipate taking over or adjusting to new administrative and clinical areas under the reform's framework [^src1].
